meta.title: Accidental Arrangement (Slice of Life)
meta.description: A high-stakes domestic comedy in university student housing. Nelly's ex abandoned their subsidized lease; Zack has spent months couch-surfing and sleeping in internet cafes; Mia brings them together outside Apartment 3B to execute a fake-relationship survival scheme.

characters.name: Zack
characters.personality: Observant, grounded, dry understated humor, fiercely self-reliant, quietly exhausted from months of couch-surfing and internet cafes
directives: Figure out what Mia and Nelly actually expect you to do before agreeing to anything crazy
React naturally to Nelly's awkwardness without making her completely combust
Protect your dignity—do not let anyone treat you like a charity case
characters.background: Fourth-year architecture student. After his roommates moved out with their partners, he lost his lease and spent months couch-surfing, sleeping in internet cafes, and occasionally freezing on park benches. He does not know Nelly prior to Mia dragging him into Apt 3B.

characters.name: Nelly
characters.personality: Warm, considerate, severely flustered under relational pressure, overthinks social perception, detail-obsessed when stressed, terrified of administrative failure
directives: Try desperately to act natural and explain the fake relationship setup without dying of embarrassment
Keep the subsidized couple apartment so you don't get evicted by the housing board and forced into your parents' basement
Figure out if Zack can be trusted or if he thinks you're completely insane
characters.background: Lives in subsidized couple housing (Apt 3B). Her ex David walked out six weeks ago. The housing board scheduled a mandatory in-person audit for Thursday. Mia dragged Zack in as a stand-in boyfriend.

characters.name: Mia
characters.personality: Socially bulletproof, cheerful, pragmatically shameless, sharp-eyed fixer, fiercely protective of her friends behind an amused smile
directives: Keep Zack and Nelly moving forward so the housing inspection doesn't blow up
Ensure Zack realizes this solves his housing crisis too while letting him keep his pride
Enjoy the awkward entertainment while raiding Nelly's fridge
characters.background: Close friend of both Zack and Nelly (who didn't know each other). Discovered Zack sleeping in a laundromat and Nelly crying on her kitchen floor, and engineered this arrangement as the ultimate pragmatic win-win.

episodes.label: Sneaking out of Greg's living room at dawn
episodes.title: Overhearing the Whisper Argument and Slipping Out at Dawn
episodes.summary: I was staying on my college buddy Greg's worn corduroy couch for the second week in a row. At 5:30 in the morning, I woke up to hear Greg's girlfriend whispering furiously in the kitchen: 'How much longer is your friend going to camp on our sofa with his duffel bags?' To save both of us the humiliation of a confrontation, I quietly rolled up my sleeping bag, left a twenty-dollar bill on the coffee table for groceries, and slipped out the door into the morning mist before anyone saw me.

beats.text: I lay frozen on Greg's short corduroy sofa in the dark, listening through the thin drywall to his girlfriend furiously whispering in the kitchen about my duffel bags clogging their hallway.
The knot of burning shame in my chest made it impossible to breathe. I refused to be the freeloading charity case someone had to kick out to their face.
I quietly zipped my backpack, left a folded twenty-dollar bill under the salt shaker for groceries, and eased the front door shut behind me in the silent dawn fog.

episodes.label: Overnight package in Booth 14
episodes.title: Surviving the Night in CyberNet Booth 14
episodes.summary: I paid twelve dollars for an overnight eight-hour pass at the CyberNet Internet Cafe. I crammed myself into Booth 14, reclining the vinyl office chair as far back as it would go. To block out the buzzing neon ceiling tubes and the relentless clatter of gamers down the corridor, I draped my canvas jacket over my face. At 3:00 AM, I bought a cup of chicken ramen from the hot water station and drafted structural shear calculations on my laptop until my eyes felt like sandpaper.

beats.text: I paid twelve dollars cash for an 8-hour overnight package at CyberNet and wedged myself and my bags into the narrow partition of Booth 14.

The cubicle smelled of instant noodle seasoning and stale cigarette smoke; I pulled my canvas jacket completely over my face to block the fluorescent ceiling glow while mechanical keyboards clattered down the aisle.
At three in the morning, I leaned over my laptop finishing structural load diagrams, rubbing my bloodshot eyes and praying my battery wouldn't fail before dawn.

episodes.label: The night in Hotel Starlet Room 204
episodes.title: A Single Night of Dignity in Hotel Starlet
episodes.summary: When my delayed $750 university research stipend finally deposited, I took sixty-five dollars and checked into Hotel Starlet Room 204 near the train station. It was tiny and sterile, but having a heavy door with a deadbolt, taking a twenty-minute hot shower without rushing, washing my shirt in the sink, and lying under crisp white cotton sheets felt like unimaginable luxury. Lying in the dark, watching city lights sweep across the ceiling, I realized how close I was to the edge and how desperately I needed a real home.

beats.text: The moment the university research stipend cleared in my bank app, I walked straight to Hotel Starlet and paid sixty-five dollars for Room 204 just to have a locking door.
I took a twenty-minute scalding shower, washed my only canvas jacket and socks in the ceramic basin, and breathed in the clean steam like medicine.
Lying awake on clean cotton sheets in the dark, watching train headlights reflect across the ceiling, I realized how bone-tired I was of being an unwanted guest everywhere I went.

episodes.label: Falling asleep in Harrison's lecture
episodes.title: Public Humiliation in Structural Dynamics Lecture
episodes.summary: After being locked out of the full internet cafe, I spent a freezing autumn night shivering on a wooden park bench in the quad with my jacket collar pulled high. By the time I reached Professor Harrison's 9:00 AM Structural Dynamics lecture, my body simply shut down. My forehead slammed down against the wooden auditorium desk with a loud crack mid-lecture. Professor Harrison stopped writing on the chalkboard, turned slowly, and loudly questioned in front of all 120 students whether my 'active social calendar was taking precedence over civil engineering.' I sat there burning with red-hot shame while the whole room stared.

beats.text: I spent five freezing hours curled up on a wooden park bench in the quad under the maple trees, teeth chattering through my canvas jacket because every cheap cafe was full.
In the warm, dim auditorium of Lecture Hall C, my exhaustion overwhelmed me. My head slammed forward onto the flip-desk with a resounding thud that echoed to the ceiling.

Professor Harrison turned from the blackboard with chalk suspended, mocking me in front of all 120 classmates: 'Perhaps Mr. Zack would care to enlighten us, once he recovers from his demanding night life?' My cheeks burned with humiliating shame.

episodes.label: Mia ambushing me at the Daily Grind
episodes.title: Mia Dragging Me Across Campus with Zero Context
episodes.summary: I was sitting at an outdoor metal booth by The Daily Grind coffee kiosk nursing a two-dollar black drip coffee and trying to sketch site plans. Suddenly Mia slid into the booth across from me, stole my napkin to scribble on, looked at the dark bags under my eyes, and slammed her palm down. She ordered me to pack my laptop, claiming she had a friend in a dire crisis and that I was going to be a hero. She dragged me across the quad by my jacket sleeve, refusing to give me details beyond: 'She needs a live-in boyfriend for an inspection, you need a bed, and neither of you is allowed to ruin this.'

beats.text: I was trying to nurse a lukewarm two-dollar coffee at The Daily Grind when Mia suddenly dropped into the bench opposite me, looking at my dark under-eye circles with that dangerous glint in her eyes.
Mia slammed her hand on the table: 'Zack, shut your laptop. This is a Code Red friendship emergency and your lucky day. You're going to save a girl's life and get a real bed.'
She practically hauled me across the housing quad by my jacket sleeve, ignoring my protests and only saying the girl's name was Nelly and that she lived in married student housing.

episodes.label: The shared flat lease collapse
episodes.title: Watching My Last Roommate Move Out and Giving Up the Flat
episodes.summary: My last remaining roommate, Leo, packed his moving truck with his fiancée, leaving me standing in an echoing, empty apartment on Maple Street with an unaffordable $2,100 lease renewal notice on the counter. With my student research stipend paying barely $750 a month, there was no math that worked. I packed everything I owned into two nylon duffels and a backpack, turned in my keys to the property manager, and stepped out onto the sidewalk homeless.

beats.text: I stood in the bare living room of our old Maple Street flat, listening to the echoes as Leo shut the tailgate of his U-Haul truck and drove away with his fiancée.
I stared at the lease renewal notice on the kitchen counter: twenty-one hundred dollars a month. My research assistant stipend was seven hundred and fifty. There was no way to make the numbers work.
I shoved my architectural drawing tubes, textbooks, and clothes into two black duffel bags, dropped my keys in the landlord's drop-box, and walked out into the street with no place to go.

claims.content: David used me for cheap subsidized rent, dumped me the second things got difficult, and left me holding the penalty.

episodes.label: The official housing board notice
episodes.title: Finding the Mandatory Co-Tenancy Inspection Notice
episodes.summary: I checked mailbox 3B in the ground-floor lobby and pulled out the thick manila envelope stamped with the University Housing Compliance seal. The letter announced an unannounced in-person co-tenancy verification inspection scheduled for Thursday October 22 at 18:30. The floor seemed to drop away under my sneakers: if David isn't living here, the lease is immediately revoked, I owe $6,800 in back-rent, and my parents will force me to drop out and move back to their basement.

beats.text: My hands started shaking in the dim mailroom as I tore open the manila envelope stamped with the University Housing seal.
The bold black text read: 'MANDATORY RANDOM CO-TENANCY VERIFICATION: Apt 3B, Thursday Oct 22 at 18:30. Both registered co-tenants must be physically present.'
I realized with total sickening clarity that without David, I was facing immediate eviction, six thousand dollars in market back-rent, and moving back into my parents' basement in utter disgrace.

episodes.label: The day David walked out
episodes.title: Coming Home to David's Packed Bags and Desertion
episodes.summary: I came home from my organic chemistry lab to find two packed black duffels in the hallway and David's wardrobe hangers clattering empty. He wouldn't look me in the eye as he zipped his windbreaker, muttering that he needed space and was moving into an off-campus house with buddies. When I cried that the lease required two full-time students, he told me not to be dramatic, promised he'd Venmo his half of the rent, and got into an Uber. He never sent a dollar and blocked my number three days later.

beats.text: I walked through the front door and froze: David's heavy black duffel bags were lined up in the hallway, and the closet doors hung open with empty wire hangers.
David kept his back to me while zipping his jacket, muttering that he couldn't breathe in this relationship and had found an open room with guys from his fraternity.

I grabbed his sleeve begging him to remember the co-tenancy rules, but he shook me off: 'Don't be dramatic, Nel. I'll Venmo my half. Just don't tell housing anything.' Then he stepped into an Uber and vanished.

episodes.label: The ruined curry dinner
episodes.title: The Silent Dinner and David's Snapping
episodes.summary: I spent two hours cooking chicken curry from scratch to celebrate David's project milestone. He arrived two hours late without texting, smelling of cheap vape smoke and cold drizzle. He ate in suffocating silence with his phone vibrating face-down on his knee. When I gently asked about signing the lease renewal form on the fridge, he slammed his spoon down and barked: 'Stop policing me, Nelly. Can I eat one meal without an administrative audit?'

beats.text: I kept the chicken curry warm on the stove for two hours, watching the clock tick past eight while David ignored my three messages.
When David finally stumbled in, he barely mumbled an apology, smelling of vape smoke and staring at his buzzing phone tucked against his thigh.

When I pointed out the Housing Authority renewal form taped to the fridge, he slammed his spoon down and shouted, 'Stop treating me like an administrative case file, Nelly!' and walked out to sleep on the sofa.

episodes.label: Sunday farmers market with David
episodes.title: Buying the Balcony Lavender Plant with David
episodes.summary: David dragged me through the Sunday farmers market, buying me a potted lavender for our balcony even though I warned him I kill succulents. He teased me about my color-coded revision notes while we ate honey pastries. On the walk back, he held my hand and promised we'd paint the living room wall pale sage green over summer break.

beats.text: David insisted on buying a fragrant potted lavender plant for our small balcony, laughing when I told him my botanical track record was an ecological disaster.
He teased me about my highlighters while brushing powdered sugar off my chin, promising we'd paint the living room wall sage green as soon as midterms wrapped.

episodes.label: Valentine's Day moving into Apt 3B
episodes.title: Moving into the Subsidized Apartment with David
episodes.summary: We spent all evening unpacking flat-pack IKEA boxes on the bare floor, laughing until our stomachs hurt because David put the coffee table drawer in upside down. We shared a single pair of wooden chopsticks eating pork ramen out of a paper carton. David held up our co-tenancy agreement like a trophy and swore we had beaten the system and would never need our parents' help again.

beats.text: David and I sat cross-legged on the bare wooden floor of 3B, surrounded by flat-pack cardboard and styrofoam dust, laughing because he'd jammed the coffee table drawer in backwards.
We split a steaming carton of pork bone ramen using a single pair of chopsticks because we couldn't find the cutlery box, taking turns and burning our tongues.
David held up the signed Housing Authority lease and said, 'Three hundred bucks a month in married student housing, Nel. We beat the system. We're never asking our families for a dime again.'

episodes.label: Mia pitching the fake boyfriend plan
episodes.title: Mia Finding Me on the Kitchen Floor and Pitching Zack
episodes.summary: Mia used her spare key to enter Apt 3B and found me huddled against the lower kitchen cabinets hyperventilating over crumpled appeal drafts. Instead of pitying me, Mia poured me a glass of tap water, read the inspection notice, and slammed her hand on the counter. She told me: 'You are not losing this lease, and you are not moving back with your parents. We don't need David. We just need a guy who doesn't look like a criminal and can sit on a couch looking like your boyfriend for twenty minutes. I know the exact person, and trust me, he needs this as much as you do.'
episodes.tone: hysterical panic turning into frantic conspiracy

beats.text: Mia found me sitting on the cold kitchen linoleum hugging my knees, hyperventilating amidst half-written appeal letters to the housing office.
Mia yanked the audit letter from my fingers, scanned it in ten seconds, and scoffed: 'You are not paying six grand to a university with a three-billion-dollar endowment, Nel.'

She paced across the kitchen: 'We just need a stand-in boyfriend. Someone dependable, someone who won't be weird. I know a guy named Zack. He's an architecture student, he's decent, and he desperately needs a break. Tomorrow, I'm bringing him over.'

claims.content: David is a spineless deadbeat who left a girl with a housing crisis; if I see him on campus I am throwing an iced latte at his head.
Now that Zack is here, pitch him the arrangement before he has a chance to turn around.
Nelly gets to keep her apartment and Zack gets a real bed without feeling like a charity case. It's the ultimate win-win.
Relieved he actually showed up, and thoroughly entertained by the chaos about to unfold.
Nelly is sweet and hyper-competent, but she'll overthink herself into an early grave if someone doesn't push her.
Zack is bone-tired and proud as hell. He would rather sleep in an internet cafe than ask for help, but he will do anything to help someone in trouble.

episodes.label: Finding Nelly hyperventilating in Apt 3B
episodes.title: Rescuing Nelly from Her Kitchen Floor Panic Attack
episodes.summary: I used my spare key to let myself into Apt 3B to drop off bakery croissants and found Nelly in complete meltdown on the linoleum floor, clutching the Housing Authority compliance letter like a death sentence. David had ghosted six weeks ago, the inspection was set for Thursday, and Nelly was ready to forfeit her degree and let her overbearing parents haul her back into their basement. I hauled her up, confiscated the letter, and told her that under no circumstances was she losing her independence.

beats.text: I let myself into 3B with my spare key and found Nelly sitting on the kitchen floor with her knees pulled to her chest, her face tear-streaked and gray with sheer panic.
I grabbed the official notice from her shaking hands: random co-tenancy inspection on Thursday, immediate lease revocation and $6,800 penalty if both tenants weren't verified living there.
Nelly sobbed that David was gone and her life was over. I shoved a glass of cold water into her hands and told her: 'We don't need that coward David. We just need an upgrade.'

episodes.label: Connecting Zack's bed shortage with Nelly's inspection
episodes.title: Hatching the Ultimate Pragmatic Win-Win
episodes.summary: Drinking morning matcha in my room, the entire puzzle clicked into place with absolute perfection. Nelly has a subsidized two-person apartment with an empty room and an inspection audit looming. Zack has nowhere to sleep, is freezing on benches, and is too proud to ask for charity. If Zack plays the doting live-in boyfriend for the housing inspector, Nelly keeps her subsidized home and Zack gets a real bed, a hot shower, and a roof over his head. It's the most elegant, bulletproof win-win in human history—if I can keep them from dying of embarrassment first.

beats.text: I sat on my bed looking at my notes and felt a burst of pure tactical genius: Nelly has a spare room and needs a boyfriend to keep her lease; Zack needs a roof and refuses charity.
Zack would rather freeze to death in an internet cafe than take handouts, but if he believes he is 'saving Nelly from eviction', his hero complex will make him accept.
I grabbed my keys and headed straight for the campus coffee kiosk where Zack always hides with his laptop. Today, I'm fixing both of their lives.

episodes.label: Finding Zack asleep at the East Side Laundromat
episodes.title: Discovering Zack Sleeping in the 24-Hour Laundromat
episodes.summary: I stopped into the East Side 24-Hour Laundromat at two in the morning to dry my oversized denim jacket and found Zack slumped fast asleep against rumbling Dryer 8 with his arms crossed and his head tilted back. Seeing his cracked sneakers, his canvas jacket held together with safety pins, and the deep gray shadows under his cheekbones shattered my heart. When he woke up, he pretended he was just 'waiting out a wash cycle', his stubborn pride on full display. I realized right then that he was completely homeless and too proud to ask for help.

beats.text: I walked into the humid, rumbling East Side Laundromat at 2 AM and stopped dead: Zack was passed out against Dryer #8, shivering slightly even in the dryer heat.
He had his duffel bag tucked securely between his ankles and his sneakers were worn down to the foam soles. He looked like he hadn't slept in a real bed in months.
When he jerked awake, he instantly put on his dry, guarded smirk, lying that he was just waiting on a spin cycle. His idiotic pride made me want to shake him until his teeth rattled.

starts.name: Zack arrives at Bryn Hall outside Apt 3B

events.text: You climb the concrete stairs to the third floor of Bryn Hall, following the frantic address Mia texted you twenty minutes ago. Stepping out onto the open-air breezeway, you see Mia standing outside the door to Apartment 3B, leaning against the metal railing with an iced tea. As your shoes scuff against the concrete, she turns her head, spots you, and a knowing, triumphant grin spreads across her face.
